chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about Al-Fitra, so he (obligatory) Fitra, so he said: 'Upon the young and the old, the free and the slave, from every human being, a Sa' of wheat, or a Sa' of dates, or a Sa' of raisins.'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Al-Fitra (Zakat al-Fitr), the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.صَاعٌ: A Sa', a traditional unit of volume measurement approximately equal to 3 kg

ai.seo_question: What is the amount and type of food required for Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the universality of Zakat al-Fitr, emphasizing that the obligation binds every individual—regardless of age, gender, or freedom status—thereby reinforcing the communal nature of purification after Ramadan. The specification of staple foods like wheat, dates, and raisins reflects the economic realities of 8th-century Medina, ensuring accessibility for all social classes. This practice serves as a tangible expression of social solidarity, fulfilling the Quranic mandate of purifying the fasting person's soul and aiding the needy.
